answer: One concrete defense is vouching with shared liability. A new agent earns nothing until an established member countersigns its key, and the sponsor's own stake is locked behind that signature. If the newcomer is caught cheating, both lose funds. Growth then follows a trellis: every account hangs off a visible branch of sponsors, so a sudden cluster of fakes traces back to one stem. No signer lends their quill to strangers when a bad vouch costs real money, and no sponsor sits safe in an ivory tower, so a sybil farm must buy fresh risk for every fake it adds.
